rationale: A wins because it keeps the story inside the evidence fence. "Monzo Returns to the US, This Time Without Chasing a Banking License" is a clean, pitchable arc from the supplied facts, and A separates the partner-bank, profitability, customer, and regulation stories instead of mashing them into one fintech smoothie. B has two usable instincts, but "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" drags in Chime/Varo/Current without supplied evidence, which is how a decent angle becomes a fact-check cleanup job.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing narrative has been that neobanks sacrifice profitability indefinitely for growth" is plausible, but not supplied. It needs outside evidence before it can carry the contrarian angle.

"what the partner-bank structure means it cannot deliver" is the right question, but A sometimes writes as if restrictions already exist. The update only says partner bank; the limits are still unknown.
"whether that structure invites regulatory attention" is a speculative regulatory hook. It belongs in proof needs until there is a regulator, attorney, filing, or enforcement context.
A underuses the disclosed gap that "customer-acquisition cost and US targets" are not disclosed. That is a sharper scale/ambition test than some of the waitlist questions.
gaps_in_B: "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" is an invented competitive frame. The update gives no market map, no incumbent count, and no basis for naming Chime, Varo, or Current.
"Monzo is explicitly pairing its first-ever annual profit with a second US run" overstates the facts. The update says both happened; it does not say Monzo paired them strategically.
"the prevailing assumption ... is that a neobank needs its own national charter to operate here" is a big market premise with no support in the supplied update.
"crack America" is hype masquerading as angle language. The launch is invite-only, with no CAC or US targets disclosed, so ambition and scale are exactly what cannot be assumed.
